original_description: Make code measurably faster or leaner without breaking it - the recursive loop of baseline → profile → one hypothesis → one change → re-measure with statistics → keep only if significant AND tests stay green, otherwise revert and record why, repeat until a stop rule fires - for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript on Node and Bun, browser pages and Bash. Pins behaviour first (tests and coverage of the changed path, kill matrix at higher rigor), records every experiment (kept or rejected) in Quest and lore, hands concurrency and algorithm-equivalence questions to proof-skills, and scales evidence with the R1-R5 rigor profiles. Use this skill whenever the user asks to speed something up, optimize, reduce latency/memory/startup/build time/bundle size/page load, says something is "slow", "takes forever", "times out" or "uses too much memory", wants a performance pass, or asks to iteratively/recursively improve performance - even if they never say "profile". For measuring or reviewing without changing code use perf-measure; for CI gates use perf-ci.
best_description: Use this skill whenever the user wants existing code made faster or leaner and expects it to be changed. That covers "optimize this", "speed it up", "make it quicker", "it's slow", "takes forever", "times out", "hot loop", "bottleneck", "too many queries", and cutting startup, build, latency, memory, bundle or page-load time. It applies to Python, JS/TS (Node, Bun), browser pages, Bash scripts and SQL- or I/O-heavy endpoints. Trigger even for short, casual requests that never mention profiling or benchmarks, and for requests with targets like "5x faster" or "tests must keep passing". It runs a measured loop: baseline, profile, one change at a time, keep only significant wins with tests green, and log every experiment. Don't use it for measure-only or "where does the time go" questions with no edits (use perf-measure), CI performance gates (use perf-ci), performance code review, explaining profiling concepts, or non-performance bugs and features.
final_description: Use this skill when the user wants their code to run faster, finish sooner, or use less memory, and expects you to edit it.
